title: Sight-reading fluency
summary: Sight-read eight new bars every sitting and count how many notes you got right the very first time.
materials: the piece from your teacher, with a pencil
a music book with pages easier than your usual pieces, for new bars each sitting

figure.alt: A row of eight boxes, standing for eight new bars sight-read once, slowly, without stopping to fix a mistake, so the number of notes played right the first time can be counted.

steps.title: Sight-reading fluency
steps.body:
Reading gets faster only by reading music you have never seen. Playing the same piece for the tenth time is practice for that piece, but it is not practice for reading. This week the new bars matter more than the pieces you already know.

1. Open a page you have never played, from an easier book, and pick out eight bars.
2. Sight-read those eight bars once, slowly, without stopping to fix anything.
3. Count how many notes you played right the first time, and write the number down.
4. Next sitting, pick a fresh eight bars and repeat, comparing the new number to the last one.

By the fourth sitting, look back at all four numbers together. The point is not a perfect score on any one day; it is whether the number is climbing over the week.

figure.alt: A row of eight boxes for a fresh set of eight bars each sitting, the count of notes played right the first time written down and compared, sitting to sitting.

steps.title: Four sittings
steps.body: Fifteen minutes each. Tick a sitting when it is done. Days do not matter; sittings do.
checklist: Sitting 1: eight new bars, sight-read once, count right notes, then an old piece
Sitting 2: eight fresh bars, sight-read once, count right notes, compare to sitting 1
Sitting 3: eight fresh bars, sight-read once, count right notes, compare again
Sitting 4: eight fresh bars, sight-read once, then this week's piece as if recording
An old piece played once, straight through, no stopping

steps.title: Record this week's version
steps.prompt: Say the piece, play it once through, then sight-read one fresh set of eight bars in the same take, hands in the frame.
